BHARATI RESEARCH STATION — SHORT TECHNICAL NOTES
SIH Research Reference
1. LOCATION & ENVIRONMENT
• Location: Larsemann Hills, Ingrid Christensen Coast, Princess Elizabeth Land, Antarctica.
• Located between Thala Fjord and Quilty Bay, east of Stornes Peninsula.
• Relatively ice-free rocky oasis bordering Prydz Bay.
• Operational area: ~2 km².
• Elevation: ~35 m above mean sea level.
• Nearby stations: Russian Progress Station and Chinese Zhongshan Station.
• Main physical access: Austral Summer (November–February).
• Winter isolation: April–October.
2. MAIN BUILDING — STRUCTURAL DETAILS
• Dimensions: 53.230 m (L) × 30.200 m (W) × 16.294 m (H).
• 134 prefabricated shipping containers.
• Total weight: 401.551 tonnes.
• Foundation: 83 GEWI injection piles.
• Wind loading: 54.3 psf dynamic gust pressure.
• Design life: ≥25 years.
• Building is elevated to reduce snow accumulation.
• Thermal envelope: PU-core steel sandwich panels.
• Windows: multi-cavity inert-gas glazing.
• Window heat-transfer coefficient: 0.6 W/(m²·K).
3. CONSTRUCTION & HISTORY
• 2006–2009: Architectural planning/design by consortium including bof Architekten, IMS Ingenieurgesellschaft and m+p consulting.
• 2010–2012: Construction; 134 containers prefabricated in Germany and shipped via Antwerp and Cape Town.
• 18 March 2012: Official commissioning.
• 2013: TechBean Systems Pvt. Ltd. involved in BMS O&M.
• 2014–2015: ISRO/NRSC established AGEOS at Bharati.
• 2016–2017: Mangala Mani became ISRO's first woman scientist to winter over at Bharati, spending 403 days in Antarctica.
• 2022: Indian Antarctic Bill established a domestic legal framework for Indian Antarctic operations.
4. BUILDING LAYOUT
GROUND FLOOR — LEVEL 1
• Laboratories
• Cold storage
• Technical workspaces
• Workshop
• Electrical infrastructure
FIRST FLOOR — LEVEL 2
• 24 single/double bedrooms
• Kitchen
• Dining room
• Library
• Fitness room
• Sauna
• Administrative offices
• Lounge
• Medical operating theatre
SECOND FLOOR — LEVEL 3 / TERRACE
• Local HVAC systems
• Scientific experiments
• Observation equipment
5. POWER GENERATION
• 3 × 100 kVA CHP generators.
• Fuel: Jet A-1.
• Total installed electrical capacity: 300 kVA.
• CHP waste heat is recovered through heat exchangers and used for station heating.
• Approximate indoor temperature: ~20°C.
• External temperatures can reach ~−40°C.
• Maximum thermal demand: 155 kWth.
• Heating system: low-temperature glycol-water circulation network.
• Heat source: recovered CHP waste heat.
POWER DISTRIBUTION
• Air Circuit Breaker: 3-pole.
• ETU20 LSIN.
• Rating: 250 A.
• Breaking capacity: 55 kA / 415 V AC.
UPS
• 2 × 60 kVA UPS systems support the Main Low Voltage Distribution system.
• Note: another source entry mentions 260 kVA UPS; this should be verified before final use.
6. POWER CONTROL & LOAD SHEDDING
• Distributed Control System (DCS) manages electrical loads.
• If a generator fails, critical systems receive priority:
  - HVAC
  - Water-pipe trace heating
  - Communications
  - Life-support systems
• Non-essential systems can be disconnected:
  - Sauna
  - Recreation
  - Other non-critical zones
IMPORTANT POWER DATA
• Generator RPM
• Oil pressure
• Exhaust temperature
• Electrical load
• Voltage/current/frequency
• Fuel consumption
• UPS status
• Breaker status
7. HVAC & AIR QUALITY
• HVAC is automated through the BMS.
• Air Handling Units (AHUs) provide:
  - Fresh air
  - Heating
  - Humidification
• CO and CO₂ sensors installed at critical locations.
AUTOMATION
• High CO₂ → increase ventilation/fresh-air intake.
• Good air quality → reduce outside-air intake to conserve heating energy.
IMPORTANT HVAC DATA
• Temperature
• Humidity
• CO
• CO₂
• Airflow
• Fan status
• Heating demand
• AHU status
8. WATER SUPPLY & DESALINATION
• Seawater desalination system uses Quilty Bay.
• Intake depth: ~12 m to avoid surface ice.
• Pump house: dedicated 10-ft container near shoreline.
• Pipeline from pump house to main building: ~300 m.
• Pipeline is insulated and protected by electrical trace heating.
CRITICAL FAILURE CHAIN
Trace-heating failure
→ Pipe freezes
→ Seawater supply stops
→ Desalination stops
→ Drinking/sanitation water affected
IMPORTANT MONITORING
• Trace-heating current
• Trace-heating resistance
• Pipeline temperature
• Pump status
• Water flow
• Water pressure
• Tank levels
• Desalination status
9. FUEL INFRASTRUCTURE
JET A-1
• Used mainly for CHP generators.
• Fuel farm capacity: 296 kL.
• Transfer distance: ~350 m.
• Transfer frequency: every 8–10 days.
• Intermediate storage tank: 13.6 kL.
• Day tank: 470 L.
• Day tank automatically feeds the power station.
FUEL MONITORING
• Tank level
• Fuel consumption
• Transfer status
• Pump status
• Leakage
• Tank temperature
• Daily burn rate
• Predicted remaining operating days
POLAR DIESEL
• Used mainly for:
  - Tracked vehicles
  - Snowmobiles/snow scooters
  - Other land transportation
10. WASTE MANAGEMENT
SOLID WASTE
• Compacted.
• Securely stored.
• Returned to India during summer resupply.
WASTEWATER/SEWAGE
• Treated internally.
POSSIBLE MONITORING
• Tank levels
• Flow rates
• Treatment status
• Pump status
• Leakage
• Remaining waste capacity
11. BUILDING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM — BMS
• Approximately 1,000 monitoring/control data points.
• TechBean Systems Pvt. Ltd. involved in O&M since 2013.
• Technologies/protocols mentioned:
  - SCADA
  - PLC
  - Modbus
  - IEC 60870-5
MAJOR BMS SUBSYSTEMS
• Water Leak Detection (WLD)
• Fire alarm
• Fire suppression
• CCTV
• Access control
• Rodent-repellent systems
12. SATELLITE GROUND STATION — AGEOS
• AGEOS = Antarctica Ground Station for Earth Observation Satellites.
• Operationalized by ISRO/NRSC around 2014–2015.
• Communication bands:
  - S-band
  - X-band
• Tracks polar-orbiting satellites.
• Receives Earth-observation data.
• Data is buffered and transmitted to NRSC, Hyderabad.
13. SCIENTIFIC MONITORING
Research/monitoring includes:
• Black Carbon aerosols
• Climate indices
• Historical weather patterns
• Seismological data
• Magnetic data
• Meteorological observations
NPDC DATASETS MENTIONED
• AWS Data — Bharati Station
• Synoptic Data from Bharti Station (2016–21)
• Black Carbon datasets
AWS DATA
• Temperature
• Pressure
• Wind
14. PERSONNEL CAPACITY
SUMMER
• Maximum capacity: ~72 personnel.
• Main building: 47.
• Emergency summer shelters: 25.
WINTER
• Approx. 24 overwintering personnel.
• Essential roles:
  - Scientists
  - Medical staff
  - Cooks
  - Mechanical/electrical personnel
HUMAN FACTOR
Winter isolation may cause:
• Circadian disruption
• Sleep problems
• Reduced concentration
• Cognitive fatigue
• Reduced decision-making performance
DIGITAL UI REQUIREMENT
• Simple navigation
• High contrast
• Clear icons
• Minimal steps
• Automation
• Prominent critical alarms
• Low cognitive load
15. LOGISTICS & AVIATION
SUPPLY CHAIN
Cape Town
→ Antarctic waters
→ Expedition vessel
→ Helicopter
→ Bharati
• Heavy cargo, fuel and equipment mainly transported during summer.
• Heavy-lift helicopter: KAMOV-32 or equivalent.
• Coaxial rotor design supports stable underslung cargo operations.
• Expedition vessel helideck: 16 × 16 m.
HELIPADS
• Total: 3
  - 2 concrete
  - 1 wooden
• Main helipad: ~900 m².
• Adjacent fueling facility.
16. GROUND TRANSPORT
VEHICLES
• PistenBully 300
• Tracked polar vehicles
• Snowmobiles
• Snow scooters
• Modified Toyota Hilux pickup trucks
USES
• Cargo movement
• Personnel movement
• Station-area logistics
• Field operations
17. MEDICAL & EMERGENCY CAPABILITY
• Medical operating theatre available.
• Winter evacuation is extremely difficult/impossible under severe isolation/weather.
• Requires adequate:
  - Medical supplies
  - Spare parts
  - Emergency equipment
  - Power redundancy
  - Communication redundancy
• Notes mention a maritime incident involving ~100 passengers evacuated to Bharati, demonstrating summer emergency/mass-casualty capability.
18. MAINTENANCE & SPARE PARTS
• O&M governed by multi-year government contracts.
• TechBean Systems Pvt. Ltd. involved with BMS O&M since 2013.
• NCPOR OMRC tender: AL-11019/1/2025.
• Normal spare-part delivery is unavailable during winter.
• Spare-part and inventory management are therefore critical.
KEY CHALLENGE
Equipment failure during winter
→ No immediate external supply
→ Dependence on onboard spare parts
→ Local repair capability required
19. CURRENT DIGITAL ECOSYSTEM
CURRENT FLOW
Sensors
→ PLC/SCADA
→ BMS
→ Local alarms/control
• Approximately 1,000 data/control points.
• Data is heavily localized.
• Remote headquarters visibility may be fragmented.
• Potential improvement: unified real-time command-and-control dashboard.
20. PROPOSED DIGITAL PLATFORM
A. SEAWATER INTAKE PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE
Monitor:
• Current
• Resistance
• Pipe temperature
• Water flow
• Pump status
ML anomaly detection:
• Detect abnormal electrical behavior.
• Predict trace-heating failure.
• Warn before pipeline freezing.
B. GENERATOR PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE
Monitor:
• RPM
• Oil pressure
• Exhaust temperature
• Electrical output
• Fuel consumption
• Operating hours
Purpose:
• Detect component degradation.
• Predict maintenance requirements.
• Reduce unexpected winter failures.
C. HVAC OPTIMIZATION
Combine:
• Indoor CO/CO₂
• HVAC data
• External AWS/weather data
• Temperature
• Wind
• Occupancy
Purpose:
• Predict heating demand.
• Optimize HVAC.
• Reduce Jet A-1 consumption.
D. FUEL BURN-RATE MODELING
Track:
• Current fuel level
• Daily consumption
• Consumption trend
• Remaining operating days
• Transfer frequency
• Predicted resupply requirement
Track separately:
• Jet A-1
• Polar Diesel
21. OFFLINE-FIRST ARCHITECTURE
PROBLEM
Communication may be disrupted because of:
• Weather
• Satellite availability
• Solar conditions
• Limited bandwidth
RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE
Sensors
→ Local Edge Gateway
→ Local Database/AI
→ Local BMS Actions
→ Connectivity returns
→ Data synchronization
→ NCPOR/Goa
KEY PRINCIPLE
Safety-critical operations must continue even when cloud/remote connectivity is unavailable.
22. SECURITY & ACCESS CONTROL
USE RBAC — ROLE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL
Possible roles:
• Scientists
• Engineers
• Medical staff
• Administrators
• Station commander
• Remote NCPOR operators
CRITICAL MANUAL OVERRIDE SHOULD RECORD:
• User ID
• Timestamp
• Action
• Previous state
• New state
• Reason
Then generate:
• Immutable audit log
• Remote alert
